description: What a node of an agent graph IS. The kind decides the node's COLUMN in the layered layout (a human asks on the left, an agent answers, a resource it reads follows and a tool it calls stands on the right), its glyph, its stable data-kind hook and its localized word — which is why the member order is part of the contract. The set is deliberately small and transport-neutral: a host maps its own backend vocabulary (a participant role, a tool-server key, a document store, the human in the loop) onto these four values.

members.name: Agent
members.description: The agent that acts — a participant, a role, a runtime agent. Painted in the middle-left column, with the agent palette slot of AgentGraphNode.Agent when the host supplied one.

members.name: Tool
members.description: A tool the agent called (a tool server, a function, an MCP server). Painted to the RIGHT of the agent, because an agent-to-tool edge is what a call looks like.

members.name: Resource
members.description: A resource an agent read or wrote (a document, a table, a ledger, a memory store). Painted between the agent column and the tool column.

members.name: Human
members.description: The human in the loop — the person who asked, approved or is being waited for. Painted to the LEFT of the agents, because the request comes from there.
